candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — clinical-trial care coordination, protocol adherence, and participant safety
candidate.educational_objective: Apply the oncology clinical research nurse's role to a participant-reported adverse event by prioritizing assessment, accurate documentation, protocol adherence, prompt investigator communication, and coordinated safety care within delegated scope.

options.A: Assess and document the symptom, promptly notify the investigator/research team, follow the protocol-defined safety and adverse-event pathway, and coordinate clinically necessary care.
options.B: Independently reduce the investigational-drug dose before contacting the investigator so treatment can continue without a protocol interruption.
options.C: Wait until the next scheduled study visit to document the symptom unless the client independently decides to seek emergency care.
options.D: Omit the symptom from study documentation if it is already listed as a known adverse effect of the investigational drug.

candidate.rationale: Oncology clinical research nursing requires precise protocol adherence, adverse-event monitoring and reporting, rigorous documentation, and coordination of care. When a participant reports a new severe symptom, the research nurse should assess and document the event, promptly involve the investigator/research team, and use the study protocol's safety and reporting procedures while coordinating clinically necessary care. FDA regulations place responsibility on the investigator for conducting the study according to the investigational plan, protecting participants, maintaining accurate case histories, and reporting relevant adverse effects. A nurse should not independently alter an investigational regimen outside the protocol and delegated authority, delay evaluation of a severe symptom until a routine visit, or omit a known/expected event from required trial documentation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: ONS identifies protocol adherence, adverse-event monitoring/reporting, documentation and care coordination as core clinical research nursing responsibilities. FDA requires investigators to conduct IND studies according to the investigational plan, protect participant safety, maintain adequate and accurate case histories, and promptly report qualifying adverse effects; delegated nursing work remains within protocol and investigator oversight.
